verdict: printed reading retained; full-domain injectivity fails; exact restricted argument proves the divisibility used

source_definitions.338_5.1: A=Z[N,...,lambda^dN; x,...,lambda^jx,...], with only lambda^iN=0 for i>d.
source_definitions.338_B: B is generated over Z by N1,...,Nd with lambda^i(Nj)=0 for i>=2, hence B=Z[N1,...,Nd].
source_definitions.338_map: The displayed f:A→B is specified on N by N↦sum_i Ni; no image of x is stated.
source_definitions.339_claim: f is injective and identifies A with the ring of symmetric polynomials in the Ni.

explicit_obstruction.every_extension: A map with N↦N1 sends x to some p(N1) in B. The element x-p(N) is nonzero in the displayed independent polynomial coordinates of A and maps to0.
explicit_obstruction.concrete_lambda_map: Choose f(N)=N1 and f(x)=0. The source relations hold, so4.7 supplies the lambda-map. It kills the nonzero variable x.
explicit_obstruction.conclusion: No such full-domain map is injective for this allowed d, and the printed assertion cannot follow from the elementary-symmetric images of the N-coordinates alone.

exact_restricted_morphism.domain: A0=Z[N,lambda^2N,...,lambda^dN], the actual lambda-subring generated by N; its inclusion j:A0→A sends every coordinate to the identical coordinate.
exact_restricted_morphism.map: f0:A0→B,lambda^kN↦e_k(N1,...,Nd), defined by N↦sum_i Ni. It equals f composed with j for every extension f in the source construction.
exact_restricted_morphism.injectivity: Order N1>...>Nd lexicographically. The leading monomial of e_k is N1...Nk. Thus the leading exponent vector of e_1^{a1}...e_d^{ad} is(a1+...+ad,a2+...+ad,...,ad). The triangular map from(a1,...,ad) is injective, so distinct monomials in the independent A0 coordinates have distinct leading monomials; no nonzero polynomial relation maps to0.
exact_restricted_morphism.image: Every e_k is symmetric. Conversely a symmetric polynomial has lexicographically leading exponent vector b1>=...>=bd. Subtract its leading coefficient times e1^{b1-b2}e2^{b2-b3}...ed^{bd}. This removes the leading symmetric orbit while preserving integrality and degree. Iteration in each finite degree terminates, expressing the polynomial over Z in the e_k. Therefore the image is exactly B^{S_d}.

divisibility_verification.element: D=lambda_{-1}(N) in A0 maps to product_i(1-N_i). For p>=1 put R_p=f0(lambda^p(D)).
divisibility_verification.evaluations: For each i, e_i:B→Z[N1,...,omit Ni,...,Nd] sends Ni↦1 and every other Nj to itself. All target images are line elements, so e_i is a lambda-map by the defining relations. It sends f0(D) to0 and therefore e_i(R_p)=lambda^p(0)=0.
divisibility_verification.factor_product: Each1-N_i divides R_p by polynomial division in Ni. These factors are distinct nonassociate primes in the polynomial ring over Z; hence their product divides R_p. Write R_p=f0(D)Q_p with Q_p in B.
divisibility_verification.symmetric_descent: Both R_p and f0(D) are symmetric. For every permutation sigma, f0(D)(sigma(Q_p)-Q_p)=0. B is an integral domain and f0(D) is nonzero, so Q_p is symmetric. The proved image description gives Q_p=f0(q_p) for q_p in A0; injectivity then gives lambda^p(D)=D q_p in A0 and hence in A.
divisibility_verification.x_extension: The2.3 polynomial P_p(lambda^ix,lambda^jD) is of positive weight p in its second family. Every monomial therefore contains at least one positive lambda^j(D), each divisible by D. Consequently lambda^p(xD) is divisible by D in the full A, exactly the assertion of5.2.
